# Overview

`TG_ORA()` performs target gene enrichment analysis by testing the overlap
between a set of differentially expressed genes and each pathway's gene
set. The input gene set is the target genes of differentially expressed
miRNAs, mapped through `background_MGI`. This is a standard
over-representation analysis, built on `r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("clusterProfiler")`'s
`enricher()`.

This vignette uses the same toy BLCA example data as the package's main
Quick Start vignette. See `vignette("miREA")` for a description of that
data and for running all nine methods together through `miREA()`.

# Required inputs

* `pathway`, a two column data frame with columns `pathway` and `gene`.
* `mir_DEdata`, a four column data frame with columns `miRNA`,
  `log2FoldChange`, `stat`, and `padj`.
* `background_MGI`, a two column data frame with columns `miRNA` and
  `gene`, or `NULL` to use the bundled default (see `vignette("miREA")`,
  Step 1, for details on `background_MGI`).
* `background` for `TG_ORA()` itself, a character vector of background
  genes. If left `NULL`, `clusterProfiler::enricher()` falls back to its
  own default universe.

```{r load-data}
library(miREA)
data(toy_pathway)
data(toy_mir_DEdata)
data(toy_gene_DEdata)
data(background_MGI)
```

# Run TG-ORA

```{r prepare-input}
input_data <- getAllInputData(
    methods = "TG_ORA",
    pathway = toy_pathway,
    mir_DEdata = toy_mir_DEdata,
    gene_DEdata = toy_gene_DEdata,
    background_MGI = background_MGI
)
```

`input_data$data$TG_ORA` holds the target genes of differentially
expressed miRNAs, built by `getAllInputData()`. `input_data$pathway$TG`
holds the pathway gene sets, unchanged from the `toy_pathway` input.

```{r run-tg-ora}
res <- TG_ORA(
    TG = input_data$data$TG_ORA,
    background = unique(toy_pathway$gene),
    pathway = input_data$pathway$TG,
    pvalueCutoff = 1
)
head(res)
```

# Run through miREA()

`TG_ORA()` can also be run through the `miREA()` wrapper, which is useful
when you want its result alongside other methods' results in a single
`miREAResult` object (see `vignette("miREA")`, Step 2, for the
multi-method case). For a single target, `background` can be a plain
character vector instead of a named list.

```{r run-through-miREA}
result <- miREA(
    methods = "TG_ORA",
    input_data = input_data,
    background = unique(toy_pathway$gene),
    pvalueCutoff = 1
)
head(result$result$TG_ORA)
```

# Supplying your own miRNA list

`TG_ORA()`'s real input is a list of genes targeted by miRNAs of
interest, not a list of genes directly. If you already have a miRNA list
from an external analysis instead of letting `getAllInputData()` derive
one from `mir_DEdata`, map that miRNA list to its target genes through
`background_MGI`, the same step `getAllInputData()` performs internally,
and call `TG_ORA()` with the result.

```{r custom-list, eval=FALSE}
my_miRs <- c("hsa-miR-21-5p", "hsa-miR-155-5p") # replace with your own miRNA list
my_TG <- unique(background_MGI$gene[background_MGI$miRNA %in% my_miRs])
res_custom <- TG_ORA(
    TG = my_TG,
    background = unique(toy_pathway$gene),
    pathway = toy_pathway,
    pvalueCutoff = 1
)
```
